name: Houston
operatingHours: METRORail Red, Green and Purple lines run from ~4:30 AM to ~midnight daily (Red Line to ~2:00 AM on Friday and Saturday nights; exact times vary by station). Red runs every 6 min on weekdays and every 12 min at weekends; Green and Purple every 12–18 min. No all-night rail service.
fareInfo: Flat $1.25 per ride (2026) with free transfers to buses and other rail lines for 3 hours on the same payment. Tap a contactless bank card or phone, a RideMETRO card ($2), or use the RideMETRO app. Platform ticket machines sell 3-Hour and Day Passes. Pay before boarding; there are no faregates.

sights.name: Space Center Houston
sights.note: NASA Johnson Space Center's visitor centre: a Saturn V rocket, the shuttle carrier jet and tram tours to Mission Control. About 40 km southeast of downtown, so plan on a car or tour.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, later on weekends and in summer

sights.name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
sights.note: Dinosaur halls, a gem and mineral vault, a planetarium and the glass-cone Cockrell Butterfly Center, at the edge of Hermann Park.

sights.name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
sights.note: One of the largest art museums in the US, spread over three buildings and a sculpture garden linked by tunnels, including James Turrell's light tunnel.
sights.hours: 11:00 AM–6:00 PM Tue–Sat (Thu to 9:00 PM, free general admission), 12:30–6:00 PM Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: Daikin Park
sights.note: The Houston Astros' downtown ballpark (formerly Minute Maid Park), with a retractable roof and a full-size train above left field; behind-the-scenes tours on non-game days.
sights.hours: Open for games and scheduled ballpark tours

sights.name: Houston Zoo
sights.note: A 55-acre zoo inside Hermann Park with elephants, gorillas, a big-cat trail and a sea-lion habitat.

sights.name: National Museum of Funeral History
sights.note: A quirky, surprisingly thoughtful museum of hearses, papal funerals and mourning customs, on the far north side near IAH.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–4:00 PM Mon–Fri, 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Sat, noon–5:00 PM Sun

sights.name: Children's Museum Houston
sights.note: Hands-on galleries for kids up to about age 12, including a pint-sized city where children run the shops and the bank.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Tue–Sat, noon–6:00 PM Sun; closed Mon except summer and holidays

sights.name: Holocaust Museum Houston
sights.note: A museum of Holocaust history and human rights, with survivor testimony and a restored WWII-era railcar.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Sat, noon–5:00 PM Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: Bayou Bend Collection and Gardens
sights.note: Ima Hogg's 1920s mansion, now MFAH's collection of early American furniture and art, set in 14 acres of formal gardens beside Buffalo Bayou.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue–Sat, 1:00–5:00 PM Sun, closed Mon

sights.name: The Menil Collection
sights.note: A free museum of surrealist, modern and ancient art in a Renzo Piano building, with a campus of galleries and lawns in leafy Montrose.
sights.hours: 11:00 AM–7:00 PM Wed–Sun, closed Mon–Tue; free

sights.name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
sights.note: A 64-foot horseshoe fountain behind Williams Tower in Uptown, a short walk from the Galleria.
sights.hours: Park open ~8:00 AM–midnight; fountain runs ~9:00 AM–9:00 PM

sights.name: Discovery Green
sights.note: A 12-acre downtown park opposite the convention centre with a lake, splash pad, lawn concerts and an ice ribbon in winter.

sights.name: Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern
sights.note: A vast 1926 underground drinking-water reservoir, its 221 columns now lit for guided tours and art installations.
sights.hours: Timed tours ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM Wed–Sun (closed Mon–Tue)

sights.name: Meow Wolf's Radio Tave
sights.note: Meow Wolf's immersive art maze in a fictional radio station, opened in 2024 in the Fifth Ward next to Saint Arnold.
sights.hours: Days and times vary; check the calendar

sights.name: Buffalo Bayou Park
sights.note: A 160-acre green corridor along the bayou west of downtown, with trails, skyline views, Lost Lake and kayak rentals.

sights.name: Saint Arnold Brewing Company
sights.note: Texas's oldest craft brewery, with a beer hall, a beer garden and a self-guided tour just north of downtown.

sights.name: McGovern Centennial Gardens
sights.note: Free themed gardens in Hermann Park with a spiral garden mount for a view over the treetops; a good pairing with the zoo and museums.

sights.name: Waugh Drive Bat Colony
sights.note: About 250,000 Mexican free-tailed bats pour out from under the Waugh Drive bridge at dusk; watch for free from the bayou-side platform.
sights.hours: Emergence around sunset, best on warm evenings

railStations.name: Houston Amtrak Station
railStations.note: Amtrak's Sunset Limited runs three times a week, west to San Antonio and Los Angeles and east to New Orleans. A Thruway bus connects to the Texas Eagle at Longview. The small station on Washington Ave is ~700 m from Theater District station (Red, Green and Purple lines).
railStations.hours: Waiting room open around train and Thruway departure times; trains run to the tri-weekly timetable.

airports.name: George Bush Intercontinental Airport
airports.transitNote: Not on the rail map. METRO bus 102 Bush IAH Express to the Downtown Transit Center takes ~60 min for $1.25. Otherwise a taxi or rideshare is ~35–45 min to downtown.
airports.hours: Bus 102: first ~4:30 AM, last ~midnight. Taxis and rideshare 24 hours.

airports.name: William P. Hobby Airport
airports.transitNote: Not on the rail map. METRO bus 40 runs to downtown in ~45–60 min for $1.25. Otherwise a taxi or rideshare is ~20–25 min to downtown.
airports.hours: Bus 40: first ~4:30 AM, last ~midnight. Taxis and rideshare 24 hours.
